content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp Creole is a fragrant Creole‑style dish made with large shrimp, tomatoes, onion, sweet bell pepper, garlic and spices, but without rice. It delivers a rich, slightly spicy flavor with hints of paprika and thyme.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Creole cuisine originated in Louisiana, blending French, Spanish, African and Native American culinary traditions.
Tomatoes in Creole sauce often replace the rarer "cherry tomatoes," giving the dish a vivid color.
Shrimp cook quickly in the sauce—usually 3‑5 minutes—to keep them tender.
Traditionally Creole is served over rice, but the no‑rice version often uses cauliflower rice or quinoa for a low‑carb alternative.
The dish is commonly garnished with fresh herbs such as parsley or cilantro for added brightness.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Shrimp provide high‑quality marine protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Without rice the dish remains low‑calorie, making it suitable for energy‑restricted diets.

items.title: Contains omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Shrimp are a good source of EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Both the shrimp and the Creole spices supply B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Tomatoes and spices (paprika, garlic) contain lycopene and quercetin, helping combat free radicals.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Shrimp can trigger severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Sodium in the sauce
items.content: Traditional Creole sauce can be salty; adjust added salt to taste.

items.title: Foodborne toxins
items.content: Improperly stored shrimp may harbor bacteria that cause food poisoning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, garnished with fresh herbs. Pair it with vegetable sides, cauliflower rice, or quinoa. A squeeze of lime adds a bright acidity.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked Creole in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 1 month. Thaw in the fridge and reheat over medium heat.
